html_en:
OpenAI's "Patch the Planet" security push is the day's headline event, but beneath it runs a deeper current: the industry is quietly renegotiating what it means to be productive alongside increasingly autonomous AI.

🛡️ OpenAI Goes on Offense for Cybersecurity

The biggest news today came from Sam Altman, who announced a sweeping cybersecurity initiative framed less as a product launch and more as a mission statement:

"We want to help all companies be secure, working with the USG and the security ecosystem. The full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber is here; state of the art performance on CyberGym. Patch The Planet and Codex Security will help solve security problems instead of just finding them." — @sama

The framing — solving security problems, not just finding them — is a meaningful pivot. Security tooling has historically been a detection game; OpenAI is betting that agentic AI can close the loop from vulnerability to patch at scale. The initiative was met with enthusiasm from the developer community. @thsottiaux, who works on OpenAI's safety team, put it simply: "Let's Patch The Planet." And @steipete echoed the sentiment with a two-word endorsement that racked up over 600 likes.

🤖 What Does It Feel Like to Have an AI Teammate?

The most substantive content today came from the AI & I podcast, where Every's Dan Shipper sat down with Mike Krieger — Instagram co-founder and now Head of Anthropic Labs — to discuss what it's actually like to use Claude's forthcoming "Fable" model over weeks, not just a first-impression demo session.

Watch/Listen: How Anthropic Uses Claude Fable 5 With Mike Krieger — AI & I by Every

Krieger's account is striking for its candor about the learning curve. Even as a power user inside Anthropic, he found himself feeling like a "total newbie" when the model arrived:

"I feel like the way that I am prompting or even thinking about decomposing a task is really out of date now with this model. It's no longer — and it's even thinking about the time horizon or the sort of interactivity model — I think, has to evolve as well." — Mike Krieger

The practical upshot is a workflow that sounds less like "using software" and more like managing a junior engineer on a different timezone:

"My last two months have been full of a lot of times where I will wish Claude a good night, set it up on a pretty complex task... and wake up to — actually, it's usually done by like two in the morning... Really impressive ability to complete the swing, get itself out of the situation where it's like, okay, Mike asked me to do this complex task overnight. I got stuck because this remote service went down. I'm gonna write a scaffolded back end for it for now." — Mike Krieger

The metaphor Krieger lands on is telling: "It really feels like now it's a teammate that I can delegate a lot of work to." That's a qualitatively different claim than "it autocompletes my code" — and it has real implications for how teams will be structured around these tools.

💰 The SpaceX Playbook: Lab + Cloud = Moat

While everyone else was focused on model launches, @swyx was doing the structural analysis nobody else is:

"SpaceX has already recouped about HALF its investment in Cursor, in compute deals. The other half is paid for if Composer 3 does well. No other company is simultaneously a leading model lab + neocloud (at least where GPUs is concerned). It's a crazy effective combo iff you've adequately planned out GPU supply if in-house training 1) goes very well 2) doesn't go very well." — @swyx

The insight is underappreciated: xAI's vertical integration — training models and selling the compute — creates a flywheel that pure-play labs or pure-play clouds can't replicate. Your model investment partially self-funds through GPU sales to the very developers building on top of you. It's a hedge and a growth engine simultaneously. Worth keeping an eye on as the neocloud market matures.

🛠️ The Tooling Layer: Claude to Vercel, WebSockets, and HTML Slides

A quieter but consequential theme today: the infrastructure around AI-generated output is rapidly maturing. Guillermo Rauch announced two meaningful Vercel upgrades — one-click deployment from Claude Design artifacts, and full WebSocket support across CDN to Fluid. The Claude → Vercel pipeline in particular is a sign of how tightly the design-to-deployment loop is closing.

Meanwhile, Aaron Levie at Box made a pointed observation about where enterprise AI value actually accrues:

"Almost all AI model and agent progress is downstream from evals... The companies that are able to best understand their own (and/or customers) workflows and how well agents participate in that work will be in the best position to actually drive real automation." — @levie

On the creative tools side, @zarazhangrui published a walkthrough of her Frontend Slides skill (22k+ GitHub stars) showing how to generate polished HTML presentations with Claude Code. Watch: YouTube demo. And @ryolu_ shared her talk from Cursor Compile on "how we build in the age of AI and what doesn't change" — worth 11 minutes of your time. Watch: YouTube.

That's the digest for today. The through-line: AI is moving from tool to collaborator, and the companies building the rails — compute, deployment, evals — may matter as much as the model labs themselves.
html_zh:
OpenAI今天以网络安全为主题发布了一系列重磅更新，而AI工具链的整合浪潮也在悄然重塑着开发者的日常工作流——从代码编辑器到云部署，一键直达的时代正在到来。

🛡️ OpenAI"修补地球"：网络安全成新战场

今天最引人注目的发布来自OpenAI。CEO Sam Altman 宣布推出面向网络防御的全套方案：

"我们希望帮助所有企业保障安全，与美国政府及安全生态系统携手合作。GPT-5.5-Cyber 完整版正式上线，在 CyberGym 上达到最先进水平。Patch The Planet 与 Codex Security 将帮助解决安全问题，而不仅仅是发现问题。" —— @sama

OpenAI安全研究员 @thsottiaux 也在社交媒体上大力推广这一愿景，写道："让我们修补整个星球。Codex安全更新与全新GPT-5.5-Cyber正式发布——这是网络防御加速的庆祝之日。" 这一"进攻性网络安全"转向意义深远：AI模型正从被动的漏洞扫描工具，进化为主动修复代码的防御力量。

🔗 工具链整合：从设计稿到上线，一键搞定

如果说今天有一个让开发者最兴奋的产品动态，那就是Vercel与Claude的深度整合。Guillermo Rauch 发布了一个简短却令人印象深刻的演示：

"Claude Design → Vercel，一键部署。" —— @rauchg

与此同时，Vercel还宣布正式支持 WebSocket 与 socket.io，从CDN到Fluid全线覆盖——对于需要实时功能的AI应用而言，这是一个关键的基础设施补丁。

另一个值得关注的整合：Aaron Levie 宣布Box现在可以预览、编辑、管理版本并安全分享任意HTML内容，直接服务于AI Agent生成的产出物。"HTML又重新变得重要了，"他调侃道。

🤖 用好新模型是一门新技能：与Mike Krieger深谈Fable 5

本期最值得细读的内容，来自 Every 播客对 Anthropic Labs 负责人、Instagram联合创始人 Mike Krieger 的专访。两人探讨的核心问题是：一个真正强大的新模型上线后，你的工作方式究竟需要如何改变？

Watch/Listen: How Anthropic Uses Claude Fable 5 With Mike Krieger — AI & I by Every

"我坐在那里，感觉自己完全是个新手——我过去提示词的方式，甚至分解任务的思路，跟这个模型比起来已经完全过时了。"

Krieger 描述了他如何转变为"夜间委托"工作流：设定好上下文指令，让模型在他睡觉时完成复杂任务，通常凌晨两点就能收工。更让他印象深刻的是模型的自主应变能力：

"我遇到了很多次这样的情况——我会向Claude道晚安，把一个相当复杂的任务交给它，醒来发现它不仅完成了，甚至在某个远程服务宕机的时候，它自己搭建了一个临时的后端脚手架，记录了这一事实，等服务恢复后再修复。就是这种感觉——你可以把这种级别的任务委托出去，然后相信结果会是对的。"

这种体验的转变，正如播客主持人 Dan 所说，不仅仅发生在工程师身上——非技术背景的知识工作者同样感到"我需要一套全新的技能来使用这个模型"。

📊 Evals 才是真正的护城河

在这些炫目的产品发布背后，Box CEO Aaron Levie 发表了一段颇具洞见的长文，值得每一位企业AI决策者认真对待：

"几乎所有AI模型和Agent的进步，都源自评估体系（evals）。特定领域的开放权重微调取决于evals，应用层Agent的改进取决于evals，能真正增强工作效率的企业级Agent部署，也全部取决于evals。一切都是evals。

这将成为未来每一家企业的核心竞争力。那些能够最好地理解自身工作流、以及Agent在其中参与程度的公司，才能真正驱动自动化落地。"

这个观点或许是今天最被低估的洞见。当大家都在追逐最新模型发布时，真正的竞争差距，正在那些悄悄构建评估体系的企业里悄然拉开。

💡 编辑快讯

  • SpaceX的算盘： @swyx 指出，SpaceX通过与Cursor的算力合作，已收回约一半投资——一个模型实验室与新型云服务商合二为一的商业组合，目前无人能及。
  • Claude Code 教程： @zarazhangrui 发布了一个11分钟教程，手把手演示如何用 Claude Code 制作精美HTML演示幻灯片，其 GitHub 项目已获22k+ stars。Watch/Listen: YouTube 教程链接
  • Cursor Compile 演讲： @ryolu_ 在 Cursor Compile 大会上分享了他对"AI时代如何构建产品，以及什么永远不会改变"的思考，获得近千个点赞。
